originalTitle: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds
title: Helping Hands in Danger: Why Hospitals Must Be Safe!
content:
Hello, my wonderful friends across Africa and beyond! I'm your friendly news reporter, here to share a very important story with you today. We're going to talk about a place called Sudan, which is a big, beautiful country right here in Africa. Just like where you live, Sudan has sunshine, kind people, and lots of stories. Today, we need to talk about something a little bit sad, but it's important that we understand it. It's about hospitals. Do you know what hospitals are for?

What Are Hospitals For?

Hospitals are amazing places! They are like special houses where doctors and nurses work very hard. They help people who are sick get better. If someone falls and scrapes their knee really badly, or if they have a tummy ache that just won't go away, they go to the hospital. Doctors give them medicine and make them feel better. Nurses are also very kind helpers. They make sure everyone is comfortable and happy. They check your temperature and give you warm blankets. Hospitals are also where tiny new babies are born! It's a place full of hope and healing. Did you know? The very first hospitals were built many, many years ago! People have always known that we need special places to help those who are not well.

A Sad Story from Sudan

Now, in Sudan, there have been some grown-ups fighting. When grown-ups fight, it's very sad, and sometimes people get hurt. There is a group of grown-ups called the RSF fighters. They are one of the groups that are fighting in Sudan. It's like when kids on the playground have a disagreement, but much, much bigger and more serious. These grown-ups are fighting for different reasons, and it has made life very difficult for many people in Sudan.

Hospitals Are Being Targeted

Here's the really sad part: These RSF fighters have been hurting the hospitals. The news tells us that they have been attacking hospitals *on purpose*. This means they chose to aim at these special places where people go to get better. Imagine if someone tried to hurt your school, or your home, or the place where your grandma lives. That would be very, very wrong, wouldn't it? It's even worse when it's a hospital, because hospitals are supposed to be safe places for *everyone*. When a hospital is attacked, it means that sick children and grown-ups cannot get the help they need. Doctors and nurses get scared, and it becomes very dangerous for them to do their important work. This makes people even sicker, and it breaks our hearts. Did you know? There are special rules that all grown-ups are supposed to follow, even when they are fighting. These rules say that hospitals, doctors, and nurses must *always* be kept safe. They are never allowed to be hurt or attacked.

Why This Is So Bad

Attacking hospitals is a very, very serious problem. Think about it: If you break your arm, you need a doctor, right? If the hospital is hurt, where will you go? It stops people from getting medicine. It stops babies from being born safely. It makes a bad situation much, much worse for everyone. It makes us all feel sad and worried for the kind people in Sudan. The United Nations, which is like a very big club of countries that try to help each other, is very worried about this. There is a very kind and important man named Volker Türk. He works for the United Nations, and his job is to make sure all people are treated fairly and safely.

What Are "War Crimes"?

Volker Türk says that hurting hospitals on purpose might be something called "war crimes." Now, that's a big word, but let me explain it simply. "War crimes" mean breaking the *most important* rules during a big fight. It's like if there are rules for playing a game, and someone decides to break *all* the rules just to hurt the other players. But this is much more serious because it hurts real people and stops them from getting help. Hurting hospitals and the people inside them is one of the biggest rules to break. It means that the people who did this might have to answer for their actions because it is so wrong. Did you know? The United Nations has people all over the world who work hard to protect children and grown-ups, and to help make sure these rules are followed. They want peace for everyone.

Hope for the Future

Even though this news is sad, it's important to remember that many good people are trying to help. The United Nations and many kind people around the world are asking the fighters in Sudan to stop hurting hospitals and to remember the rules. We all hope and pray for peace in Sudan. We hope that the fighting stops soon, and that doctors and nurses can go back to helping everyone in safe hospitals. We want all children and families in Sudan to be safe and happy. Remember, kindness is very strong. Even when things are tough, we can always choose to be kind to each other and hope for a better tomorrow. Thank you for listening, my friends. Let's send our best wishes to the children and families in Sudan.
summary: In Sudan, hospitals are being attacked by fighters, which is very sad because hospitals are safe places where doctors and nurses help sick and hurt people, and a big helper from the United Nations says this might be a very serious wrong thing called 'war crimes'.
whyMatters: This is important because hospitals should always be safe places for everyone, especially when people are hurt or sick, and attacking them means many people cannot get the help they need to get better.

originalTitle: Woman with Ebola in Nigeria confirmed as wife of Swiss diplomat
title: Our Friends in Nigeria and How to Stay Super Safe!
content:
Jambo, jambo, my super duper young friends across our amazing continent of Africa! It’s your friendly news reporter, here to share some important news in a way that’s easy for everyone to understand. Today, we're talking about staying healthy and strong, especially when we hear about new sicknesses. Don't worry, we're going to learn all about it together, and I promise you, we are all doing great things to keep everyone safe!

What Is Ebola?

First, let's talk about something called Ebola. Now, that's a big word, isn't it? Ebola is a kind of sickness, like when you get a very bad cold or feel really tired. But it's a bit more serious. It makes people feel poorly, with fever, tummy aches, and just not having much energy. Just like when you feel unwell and need to rest, people with Ebola need special care from doctors and nurses. Did you know? The sickness called Ebola got its name from a river in Africa! It was first found near the Ebola River a long, long time ago. Isn't that interesting how places can give names to things?

News From Nigeria

So, what's the news? In a country called Nigeria, which is part of our big family of African nations, there was a lady who got sick with Ebola. She is a very kind lady, and her husband is someone special because he works to help people from other countries. When someone gets sick, especially with something like Ebola, doctors and nurses work super hard to help them get better. They are like superheroes in scrubs!

What About Her Husband?

Now, you might be wondering about the lady's husband. He's not sick. That's really good news! But because his wife was sick, doctors want to be extra, extra careful. So, what they did was ask him to stay in a special, quiet place, all by himself for a little while. This special place is called 'isolation.' What does 'isolation' mean? Imagine you have a special toy, and you don't want anyone else to play with it just yet because you want to make sure it's super clean and safe for everyone. That's a bit like isolation! It means staying apart from others for a short time to make sure you are healthy and don't accidentally pass any tiny germs, even if you don't feel sick at all. It's like giving germs a big 'STOP!' sign. Did you know? Sometimes, germs can hide in your body for a few days before they make you feel sick. This time is called the 'incubation period.' Doctors ask people to stay in isolation during this time, just to be super sure they are healthy and well before going back to their families and friends.

How Do We Stay Safe?

Ebola doesn't spread through the air like a normal cough or sneeze. You mostly get it from touching someone who is very, very sick, or their body fluids, like their sweat or blood. So, it's not something you can easily catch just by walking past someone. But, my smart little friends, there are super easy and powerful ways we can all help to stay safe from *all* kinds of germs, not just Ebola! * **Wash Your Hands!** This is like having a superpower! Use soap and clean water and scrub your hands for as long as it takes to sing 'Happy Birthday' twice! Get between your fingers, your thumbs, and the back of your hands. Washing hands chases away all those tiny, invisible germs! * **Don't Touch Your Face!** Try not to touch your eyes, nose, or mouth with your hands, especially if you haven't washed them. Germs love to sneak into our bodies through these places. Keep those hands away! * **Cover Your Coughs and Sneezes!** If you need to cough or sneeze, do it into your elbow, like a little bat wing! This stops germs from flying into the air and keeps everyone around you safe. It's polite, too! * **Stay Home When You're Not Well!** If you feel sick, tell a grown-up and stay home from school or playing with friends. This helps you get better faster and stops any germs you might have from going to other people. Your body needs rest to fight off sickness.

Doctors Are Our Heroes!

We are so lucky to have amazing doctors, nurses, and scientists. They are working hard every single day to understand sicknesses like Ebola and to find the best ways to help people get better. They wear special suits that look a bit like astronaut suits to protect themselves while they care for sick people. They are very brave and clever! Did you know? Scientists around the world are always trying to find new medicines and ways to stop sicknesses. They are like super detectives, solving mysteries to keep us healthy!

Together We Are Strong!

Remember, my little superstars, our continent of Africa is full of strong, kind, and brilliant people. When we work together, listen to our parents and teachers, and practice good hygiene, we keep ourselves and our communities safe and healthy. There's no need to be scared, just smart and careful. Keep washing those hands, keep smiling, and keep learning! We'll keep you updated with more good news about staying healthy. Be well, my friends!
summary: A lady in Nigeria got sick with Ebola, but her husband is safe in a special place called isolation to make sure he stays healthy and doesn't spread germs, while doctors work hard to keep everyone well.
whyMatters: This news matters because it teaches us about staying healthy, like washing our hands, and shows how doctors and families work together to keep everyone safe from sickness, making sure we all live in a healthy community.

originalTitle: World champion Jepchirchir fails drugs test
title: News About Our Running Star, Peres!
content:
Hello, Young Champions!

Hi everyone! It's your kid-friendly reporter here, bringing you some exciting and also a little bit serious news from the world of running. We love watching our heroes run super fast, don't we? They inspire us to dream big and work hard. Today, we're going to talk about one of our amazing running stars from Africa, a super speedy lady named Peres Jepchirchir! Peres Jepchirchir is a name many of you might know. She is a truly incredible runner, one of the fastest in the whole world! Peres has won very big races, like the marathon. Imagine running for so, so long – it's like running from your house to a town far, far away, and then back again, maybe even twice! That's how long a marathon is! She has been a world champion, which means she was the very best in the entire world at her race. When she runs, she makes us all feel so proud. Her legs move like lightning, and her heart is full of courage. She trained for many years, running every single day, to become so strong and so fast. Her victories have brought so much joy and celebration to our continent. She shows us that with hard work and dedication, we can achieve anything we set our minds to.

What is a Champion?

A champion is someone who works very, very hard to be the best at something. They train every day, eat healthy food, and listen to their coaches. They never give up, even when things are tough. Peres is a champion because she did all these things. She ran up hills, she ran in the sunshine, and she ran when it was windy. She practiced her breathing and made her legs super strong. Being a champion isn't just about winning; it's about the journey and all the effort you put in. It's about inspiring others to try their best too. When Peres crosses the finish line first, she is not just winning for herself, but for all of us who cheer for her. Did you know? The word "marathon" comes from an old story about a messenger who ran a very long way to deliver important news! Today, a marathon race is exactly 42.195 kilometers long! That's a super long run!

Rules are Important in Every Game

Now, imagine you are playing a game with your friends, like football or tag. What happens if someone doesn't follow the rules? Maybe someone kicks the ball with their hand in football, or someone touches you in tag when they're not supposed to. It doesn't feel fair, does it? It can make the game not fun anymore. Well, just like in your games, big sports like running have rules too! These rules are super important to make sure everyone plays fairly and safely. They help make sure that the fastest person wins because they trained the hardest, not because they had a special "helper." These rules are made by people called the Athletics Integrity Unit. Their job is to make sure sports are fair and honest for everyone. Did you know? In sports, "fair play" means playing by the rules, respecting your opponents, and always trying your best! It's about being a good sport, whether you win or lose.

A Special "Helper" That's Not Allowed

Recently, something happened with our champion, Peres. When athletes run in big races, they sometimes have to give a tiny sample, like a little bit of their pee. Doctors check this sample very carefully to make sure no one has used any "special helpers" that are against the rules. These special helpers are called "banned substances." It's like a secret shortcut that some people might try to use to get ahead. The doctors found something in Peres's sample. They found a special helper called EPO. Now, what is EPO? It's like a special kind of medicine that can make your body carry more oxygen. Imagine oxygen is like super fuel for your muscles! If your muscles get more super fuel, you can run faster and not get tired so quickly. It's like having a secret turbo button! But this "turbo button" isn't allowed because it's not fair to other runners who are just using their natural strength and hard work. Using EPO also isn't good for your body in the long run. It can be very unhealthy. Did you know? Our bodies naturally make red blood cells that carry oxygen. EPO is a medicine that makes your body make *more* red blood cells, which means more oxygen can go to your muscles! But when it's used in sports without a doctor's permission, it's considered cheating.

Why is it Not Allowed?

Think about it this way: if one runner uses a secret turbo button and another runner doesn't, is that a fair race? No, it's not. The rules are there so that everyone starts with the same chance. The winner should be the one who trained the hardest and was naturally the strongest and fastest on that day. Using banned substances like EPO takes away that fairness. It means someone might win not because they were truly the best, but because they had an unfair advantage. It also protects the runners' health, because some of these substances can be very dangerous for their bodies. It’s important to stay healthy and strong through good food, exercise, and rest, not through shortcuts.

What Happens Now?

Because of this, Peres has been "provisionally suspended." What does that mean? It means she cannot run in any big races right now while everyone figures out what happened. It's like when you might be on a "time-out" at school to think about what you did. This is a sad time for Peres and for her fans, because we all love to watch her run. The people who make the rules will talk to Peres and listen to her side of the story. They will check everything very carefully. We hope that she will be able to run again soon. Sometimes, mistakes happen, or people might not know exactly what was in something they took. Did you know? Athletes have special doctors and nutritionists who help them make sure everything they eat or take is safe and allowed. It's a very big responsibility!

Learning and Moving Forward

This news reminds us how important it is to always follow the rules, in sports and in life. It teaches us about fair play and being honest. Even our heroes, like Peres, can face challenges. But the most important thing is to learn from challenges and keep moving forward. Peres is a strong woman, and we know she will face this challenge with courage. We still believe in her and remember all the amazing races she has run. We hope she stays healthy and continues to be an inspiration. Let's always remember that real champions are made through hard work, dedication, and always playing fair. That's the best way to win, and it's the best way to live too! Let's keep cheering for all our African heroes and for fair play in sports! Did you know? Many of the world's best long-distance runners come from East Africa, especially countries like Kenya and Ethiopia! Their amazing talent and training help them achieve incredible speeds and endurance.
summary: A famous African runner, Peres Jepchirchir, is temporarily paused from racing because a test found a special substance not allowed in fair sports.
whyMatters: This news is important because it shows us that following rules makes sports fair for everyone, and it reminds us that true champions get their wins from hard work and natural talent, which is the healthiest and best way.
